status: Read-only design preparation during Task 157 CI; no implementation or worktree yet.
design: Separate Python helper, supplied already-owned parent/run/daemon/browser directory handles. Caller context is not live authority.
Duplicate read-only directory handles with CLOEXEC; bind named entry, held identity, parent and mount; exact fixed topology.
Open eight fixed counter/event interfaces per scope read-only/no-follow/nonblocking/CLOEXEC before snapshots; preserve open failures, never silently reopen missing counters.
Keep descriptors for complete caller-owned lifetime; capture all scopes in daemon/browser/run order with per-interface and aggregate monotonic windows.
Bound each raw read to 4096 bytes plus one overflow sentinel; preserve exact bytes, explicit bounded errors and incomplete prefixes without normalizing or zero filling.
A generic capture never asserts terminal/all-exited/fsynced/ownership/qualification; later adapter must bind actual exit and durable-retention evidence.
Partial failure keeps successful raw fields available to the existing offline assessor; replacement cannot attribute reads to a new directory.
Close every owned duplicate/interface on construction failure, normal close or context exception; never close caller handles.
Only temporary filesystem fixtures and injected clocks/failures; Node wrapper can assess compatible snapshots with explicitly synthetic lifecycle declarations.
prospectiveCases: exact raw scalar/event bytes and eight fixed interfaces
4096-byte inclusive bound and 4097-byte rejection with retained prefix
open/read errors retain other successful fields
same held interfaces across observations without reopen
named counter and directory replacement; symlinks and FIFO rejection
compatibility with offline assessor PASS, known breach plus missing read, and missing terminal never filled from earlier observation

primarySources.finding: memory.peak and memory.swap.peak are creation-to-current maxima unless reset by a nonempty write for that FD; reader must never write/reset.
Use relative fixed-name reads under held directory FDs with read-only, no-follow, close-on-exec and nonblocking flags; check types and identities independently.
pread uses an explicit offset without changing the open file description offset; retain partial reads/errors and bounded windows.

remainingDesignChecks: Do not imply retained FDs keep a removed cgroup readable; named replacement/removal and failed counter reads remain unavailable.
Do not treat caller-provided boot/clock/ownership context as attested live authority.
Separate raw byte records and assessor projection: failed or oversized reads retain bounded bytes/error but do not become complete scalar fields.
No final/last-exit/fsynced claims in generic capture; live adapter must establish those independently.
Counter open failures remain sticky for that reader; no reopen after application start.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Exact raw values, stable held identities and daemon/browser/run ordered windows; no live qualification.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: Counter missing at construction, later appears
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Sticky missing-interface evidence; no reopen and no zero substitution.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: One final counter read fails after successful prior observations
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Only current complete fields enter assessor projection; unavailable field stays absent; prior complete capture unchanged.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: Known final peak excess plus another missing final field
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Existing assessor retains FAIL and separate missing-evidence reasons.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: Counter or scope name replaced while original FD remains open
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Identity conflict retained; no read attributed to replacement.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: Symlink, FIFO, directory or device at a counter name
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Rejected without blocking or following the link.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: One-byte short reads up to 4096 bytes and EOF
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Complete original bytes retained exactly within a bounded number of reads.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: 4097th byte or interrupted read after prefix
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Bounded prefix and explicit incompleteness retained; no complete raw scalar emitted.
Exact bounded bytes remain available separately; no fabricated UTF-8 scalar.
No valid observation window is manufactured; retain explicit timing failure.
Every owned duplicate/interface closes; caller-owned directory handles remain valid.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: Writable, inheritable or ambiguous original directory handles
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Reject admission without changing caller flags.
Reject before uncontrolled opening; fixed schema only.

prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.case: Two generic captures without supplied actual exits
prospectiveExpectedOutcomes.expected: Neither capture claims terminal retention, allExited, fsynced, ownership or executor qualification.

ownershipNotes: Counter ownership UID need not equal the delegated directory UID; record identities and read permissions, do not invent a same-owner rule for every cgroup interface.
Retaining an FD does not prevent group removal or guarantee readable counters; a future service must keep its owned lifetime until fsync.
